newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Approval for Iraqi food plan expected Monday.
newsitem.headline: Approval for Iraqi food plan expected Monday.

text.p: The United Nations is expected on Monday to approve a food and medical distribution plan for Iraq after a letter from U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan goes to the Security Council.
Iraq has said it would not resume exporting oil until the plan is approved.

U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said Annan had endorsed the plan on Friday but a formal letter under his name would not be sent to Security Council President Sir John Weston of Britain until the Department of Humanitarian Affairs had reviewed the plan.
The letter is expected to say Annan had informed Iraq of approval of the plan and the list of goods allowed to be imported would then be sent to the Council's sanctions committee on Iraq.

At issue is a 680-page plan in which Iraq has outlined how it will distribute food and medicine purchased under an oil-for-food-program that went into effect last December. This plan allows Iraq to sell up to $2 billion worth of oil every six months to buy food and medicine.
